tools.name: fileforge_audit_action
tools.title: Audit
tools.description: Audit a page or site for SEO, content, policy and client-side security issues. Prefer query_audit with a preset; compare_runs shows what changed between stored audits. Use fileforge_a11y_action, fileforge_perf_action or fileforge_responsive_action for one focused check. reveal_client_security_value needs FILEFORGE_ALLOW_SECRET_REVEAL=1. Results can be stored. Needs the extension.

action.description: What to do. Required parameters are in brackets. query_audit: Unified GraphQL-feel audit. Select audit modules (seo, accessibility, performance, conversion, visual, technical, privacyTrust, structuredData, crawl), presets, scores, issues, roadmap, report, and snapshots in one call. compare_audit_snapshots (beforeSnapshotId, afterSnapshotId): Compare two audit snapshots (by ID) and report score deltas, new issues, resolved issues, and changed modules. site_route (url): Audit site routes and links for broken routes, invalid links, duplicate titles, missing canonicals, redirects, and route health. content_consistency (url): Detect pricing, subscription, feature-count, product-identity, and limitation contradictions across crawled pages. extension_policy (url): Review site/listing/manifest copy for Chrome extension policy and claim-safety risks. client_side_security (url): Inspect client-side storage for Pro/license flags, exposed secrets, debug flags, tokens, and sensitive state with redacted evidence. reveal_client_security_value (url): Reveal one exact redacted client-storage value after an explicit scoped agent request, and log the reveal. recommendations_rank: Deduplicate and rank issues by impact, severity, confidence, project type, and affected pages. compare_runs (beforeRef, afterRef): Compare two stored audit runs for added/resolved issues and high-level performance/evidence changes. export_package (ref): Export a stored audit result as a ZIP package with report.md, issues.json, summary.json, and evidence/result.json. summary (ref): Return a stored audit result in an agent-friendly summary mode such as developer, seo, compliance, conversion, detailed, short, or json-only. sensitive_session_check (url): Classify whether a URL appears sensitive/private before deep authenticated-page scraping.

tools.name: fileforge_browser_action
tools.title: Browser
tools.description: Manage tabs and read browser state: go to a URL, switch, reload and close tabs, move through history, wait for a page, and list open tabs. Use query_context to see what's open, and fileforge_page_interaction to act inside a page. Closing tabs can lose unsaved work, and close_tabs_matching can close many at once, so try dryRun first. Sensitive tab URLs are redacted. Needs the extension.

action.description: What to do. Required parameters are in brackets. navigate (url): Go to a URL in a tab, or in a new tab with newTab. open_url_with_capture (url): Open a URL with capture on and return what it loaded. Closes the tab afterwards unless keepOpen is set, and stores the result by default. activate_tab (tabId): Switch to a tab. close_tab (tabId): Close a tab. Unsaved work in it is lost. reload_tab: Reload a tab, optionally bypassing the cache. history: Go back or forward in a tab. Goes back unless direction says otherwise. wait: Wait until a tab reaches until: load (the default), idle, or url, which also needs urlIncludes. query_context: Read open tabs, windows and the active tab, using a preset or a query. Changes nothing. close_tabs_matching: Close tabs matching urlIncludes or titleIncludes. Use dryRun to preview; keepActiveTab is on by default.

tools.name: fileforge_eye_action
tools.title: Eye
tools.description: Monitor many tabs at once: network traffic, console errors, JS exceptions, DOM changes and WebSocket frames. Set tripwires such as "status >= 500", then read get_tripwires; they don't notify you. watch_person tags events that mention an identity. Use fileforge_devtools_action for one tab in depth. Attaches the debugger to watched tabs; the incognito actions open and close windows. Needs the extension.

Requires tabs or all: true. stop_watch: Detach from all watched tabs and stop the live capture session. Returns a session summary. get_feed: Pull the live event feed from the active watch session — all network traffic, console messages, errors, and DOM changes across every watched tab, sorted newest-first. lock_target (tabId): Lock onto a specific tab as the primary target. On a locked tab, JS errors trigger an automatic screenshot so you can see exactly what the user saw when things broke. unlock_target: Release the current target lock and return to standard multi-tab monitoring. set_tripwire (tripwire): Plant a tripwire that fires silently the moment a matching event hits any watched tab. Check get_tripwires to see which ones have fired. get_tripwires: List all active tripwires and whether any have fired, including the timestamp and event that triggered them. clear_tripwire (tripwireId): Remove a tripwire by its ID. get_status: Get current God's Eye session status: whether a watch is active, how many tabs are watched, which tab is locked, event count, and tripwire summary. auto_track: Auto-attach to every newly-created or newly-navigated http(s) tab while the watch is active. tools.name: fileforge_task_action
tools.title: Task
tools.description: Run multi-step work two ways. Tasks (start, add, status, monitor_page) track one job. Routines (create, validate, dry_run, run, plan_from_prompt) are saved and can be scheduled, but cron only fires while this server runs. For a single step, call the tool directly. Runs act in your browser, pausing only at steps that require approval. delete removes a task; routines can only be disabled.

action.description: What to do. Required parameters are in brackets. start: Start an asynchronous task made of structured FileForge tool invocations. add (actions): Add a saved task made of structured FileForge tool invocations. edit (taskId): Edit a saved task record. status (taskId): Get the current status of a running task. events (taskId): Get progress events for a task. pause (taskId): Pause a running task. resume (taskId): Resume a paused task. cancel (taskId): Cancel a running task. list: List all tasks (running, paused, completed). delete (taskId): Delete a task and its event history. export (taskId): Export task results and artifacts. monitor_page (url): Monitor a page for changes over time. collect_table (url): Collect rows from a paginated table into a local dataset. collect_search_results (url, query): Run a search on a website and collect all results into a dataset. create (name): Create a routine (prompt or steps input). update (routineId, patch): Update a routine (snapshots a new version). get (routineId): Fetch a routine (optionally a specific version). duplicate (routineId): Duplicate an existing routine. enable (routineId): Enable a routine. disable (routineId): Disable a routine. validate: Validate a routine or an arbitrary step array against the tool catalog. dry_run (routineId): Produce a dry-run report for a routine without executing anything. run (routineId): Enqueue a routine for execution. stop (runId): Stop / cancel a running or queued run. get_runs (routineId): List runs for a routine. get_run_details (runId): Get full details of a run (steps + events + artifacts). export_run (runId): Export a run as JSON or CSV. get_tool_registry: Return the FileForge tool capability catalog. plan_from_prompt (prompt): Return planning context (registry slice + schema + planning prompt) for an LLM to use when converting a prompt into an executable step array. commit_plan (plannedSteps): Validate an LLM-produced step array and save it as a routine (new or updated).
